New satellite imagery shows additional towers and platforms around the complex as Russia continues expanding production of drones used against Ukraine.

‘Humanitarian’: Trump Weighs In on Putin Praise Amid Backlash — Donald Trump offered a qualified response when asked whether he agreed with envoy Steve Witkoff’s description of Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian.” He suggested the term could apply to the release of American detainee Stephen Hubbard but declined to give a broader assessment. Finland to Invest in Anti-Personnel Mines After Ottawa Convention Withdrawal — Finland formally withdrew from the Ottawa Convention, the anti-personnel landmine (APL) ban, in January because of the perceived growing threat from Moscow. ‘We Outplayed Them’: Ukraine Claims First Underground Counteroffensive — Ukraine’s Khartiia Corps says Operation Veles sent troops through underground infrastructure to strike behind Russian lines and disrupt a threat to Kupiansk. Buyer and Supplier: How China Sustains Russia’s War — China’s part in sustaining Russia’s wartime economy goes well beyond that of a major trading partner. ‘Red Line Crossed’: Germany Raises Russian Sabotage Threat to ‘Significant’ for First Time — Germany’s armed forces have raised the Russian sabotage threat to “significant,” the military’s second-highest internal alert level, after an explosives-carrying drone was found near Wunstorf air base. Berlin is strengthening site-specific security measures amid concerns over Russian hybrid warfare.

Russian Attacks Kill 4 Civilians, Injure at Least a Dozen Across Ukraine in Overnight Drone Strike — Russian attacks killed 4 civilians and injured at least 14 others in Donetsk, Kharkiv, Chernihiv regions, including two boys aged 10 and 13. 630 Drones Toward Moscow, Russian Military Repair Plant Reportedly Hit — Moscow Mayor claimed 630 drones had been heading toward Moscow since Oct. 21, while footage analyzed by Astra suggests a strike hit the 75th Arsenal military repair plant in Serpukhov. Russian officials also reported drone attacks and damage across several other regions.

Kremlin Confirms Lukoil Negotiations With Washington — The Kremlin confirmed talks with Washington over sanctioned Russian oil giant Lukoil’s $22 billion foreign assets, as the US Treasury extended authorization for sale negotiations until Nov. 21.

Witkoff Reveals US Treasury Working With Putin’s Envoy on Economic Ties — Witkoff confirmed direct US Treasury talks with Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev on economic cooperation alongside Ukraine peace negotiations. Putin outlined Russian diesel shipments to the US and offered fertilizer exports.

‘Capitulating to a Dictator Shows Weakness’ – Republican Senator Slams Trump’s Russia Policy — Republican Senator John Curtis criticized President Donald Trump’s Russia policy, warning that sanctions relief, Russian energy purchases and restrictions affecting Ukraine’s military capabilities are emboldening Vladimir Putin. Drawing on his recent visit to Ukraine, Curtis called for stronger American leadership and continued support for Kyiv.

Trump Envoy Grilled for Calling Putin a ‘Humanitarian’ — US special envoy Steve Witkoff sparked criticism from Republican lawmakers after calling Vladimir Putin a “humanitarian” during talks in St. Petersburg. Senator Thom Tillis sharply rebuked the envoy, while President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance defended his remarks following the release of an American detainee.

Russia Pounds Kyiv in Overnight Missile and Drone Barrage – 1 Dead, 24 Injured, Including 4 Children — Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks on Kyiv killed one person and injured 24 others, including 4 children. Strikes damaged metro infrastructure on the South Bridge, an ambulance station, six emergency vehicles, homes and businesses.

Zelensky Confirms Trilateral Talks With US, Russia Could Take Place by Early November — President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday, Oct. 21, that Kyiv had received feedback from Washington after senior US envoy Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg, with Russia signaling support for trilateral talks at the level of negotiating teams. The talks could take place by early November, though no dates have been set.

Bundeswehr Raises Threat Level, Warns of Potential Russian Attacks — German’s armed forces are concerned about the possibility of Russian sabotage attacks aimed at its personnel in Germany. As a result, it has raised the threat level for both military bases and serving individuals to “Serious,” its second-highest level.

Italy Investigates Russia’s Possible Role in Violent Protests — Italy’s government, led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, is investigating whether Russia or other foreign actors played any role in violent weekend protests in Milan and other cities. Defense Minister Guido Crosetto blamed “hybrid warfare” spread through social media, as Rome deploys military personnel ahead of new demonstrations.

Ukraine Counts on Beijing’s ‘Constructive Role’ as Sybiha Meets Chinese Ambassador — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha met with Chinese Ambassador Ma Shengkun in Kyiv on Wednesday to discuss steps Beijing could take toward peace and to revive bilateral dialogue ahead of the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Inside a Ukrainian Minefield Rescue | Drone Footage & Exclusive Interviews — In exclusive Kyiv Post interviews, combat medic “Osa” and platoon commander “Kamaro” describe reaching two soldiers wounded by a mine blast and carrying them across a minefield. Drone footage captures the evacuation, while their accounts reveal the fear, exhaustion and urgent decisions behind it.

29 Russian Troops Captured, 108 Eliminated, 1,100+ Targets Hit: Ukraine’s HUR Summarizes Sumy Operation — HUR says its special forces captured 29 Russian soldiers, neutralized 108 others and struck more than 1,100 targets during a seven-week operation in the Sumy region. The operation also cleared more than 600 hectares (almost 1,500 acres) of forest of Russian troops and thwarted Russian plans to cut off Ukrainian logistics routes.

Putin ‘Ready’ for Three-Way Ukraine Talks in November, Kremlin Says — Russian leader Vladimir Putin told US envoy Steve Witkoff that Russia was ready in principle to resume three-way negotiations with Ukraine and the United States around mid-November, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said. Moscow wants the discussions to focus on postwar security arrangements for Russia and Ukraine. The announcement followed Witkoff’s talks with Ukrainian and European leaders in Oslo.

‘We Need to Move On’: Zelensky Won’t Wait in Oslo for Witkoff After Putin Meeting — Zelensky said he would not wait in Oslo for US envoy Witkoff to return from talks with Putin and plans to head back to Ukraine. Witkoff is expected to brief Norway’s prime minister on the meeting.

European Parliament Vice President Declares Hunger Strike in Solidarity With Oleshky Residents — European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno declared a hunger strike on Tuesday, Oct. 20, in protest over the starvation of civilians in the Russian-occupied Oleshky, Kherson region. Her move followed the Vatican's latest push for a humanitarian ceasefire in the town. Kyiv’s Donors Expected Peace in 2027, but Russian Escalations Left 2026 Funding Unfulfilled — Ukraine’s allies budgeted the country’s aid through 2027 expecting a peace deal with Russia, but Moscow’s deadlier strikes pushed defense and social wage needs above what the finance ministry planned to spend. If Kyiv fails to secure aid for two months of 2026 and for 2027, the country will lack funds to pay the military, social wages and recovery projects.

Russian Su-30 Crashes Near NATO Borders, Pilots Eject — On Wednesday, a Russian jet crashed during a training flight in Kaliningrad, with both crew members ejecting and surviving, according to Russia’s defense ministry. Russian media identified the aircraft as a Su-30SM and reported that both pilots were injured. The ministry said the aircraft was unarmed and came down in an uninhabited area.

Ukraine May Have 300-500 Russian Spies Working for Kyiv — A man coordinating surveillance for Ukrainian intelligence estimates that 300-500 Russians may be doing similar work for Kyiv. HUR confirmed his cooperation with the agency, but the BBC could not independently verify the figure.

Are Russian Bots Fueling Unrest in France? — According to the Financial Times, EU regulators are investigating the possibility that “online interference” from Moscow, Tehran, and Algiers is helping to foment unrest in France. Bots are believed to be spreading claims and fake news reports suggesting that the country is descending into chaos.

Moldova Considers Moving Ukrainian Border Checkpoints Onto Its Territory — Moldova is considering relocating Ukrainian border checkpoints to its territory because of Russian attacks near the border, Chișinău’s Interior Minister Daniela Misail-Nikitin said in comments published Oct. 21. Russian drones have struck the checkpoints in recent months and led to deaths and injuries.

Putin Delays Trump’s Controversial Diesel Deal Delivery 1 or 2 Days — Vladimir Putin said Russia’s first diesel tanker under its agreement with Witkoff and Trump would depart in two to three days, revising an earlier announcement of an Oct. 22 departure. The cargo will carry 40,000 metric tons (about 44,100 US tons), approximately 13% of the initial volume announced by Donald Trump. Moscow says further shipments will follow.

Fact-Checked: Trump’s Latest Ukraine Claims — Trump claimed Russia is steadily advancing in Ukraine, has virtually unlimited manpower, the US has provided Ukraine with $350 billion in aid, and that Javelin missiles supplied during his first term were decisive in saving Kyiv in 2022.

Why the US Needs Ukraine as Much as Ukraine Needs the US — Recent decisions by the Trump administration, including its abrupt suspension of intelligence support for Kyiv, have contributed to Russian gains and Ukrainian civilian deaths. ‘He Just Doesn’t Like Him’: Trump’s Personal Animosity Toward Zelensky May Be Shaping US Policy on Ukraine — European officials and diplomats believe Trump’s personal animosity toward Zelensky is influencing Washington’s approach to Russia’s war against Ukraine. Trump Envoy Witkoff Calls Putin a ‘Humanist’ Amid Deadly Russian Attacks on Ukraine — US envoy Steve Witkoff called Putin a “humanist” while seeking the Russian leader’s support for renewed Ukraine peace talks. Meanwhile, UN monitors documented mounting civilian deaths from Russian attacks.

Putin Orders US Teacher’s Release as Witkoff Arrives for Talks — Putin ordered the release of Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American whom Washington considered wrongfully detained, Russian state media reported. The announcement coincided with Witkoff’s visit to St. Petersburg and followed Trump’s personal appeal.

Rubio: Musk Sets Ukraine’s Starlink Access, Not White House — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said SpaceX and Elon Musk determine Ukraine’s access to Starlink under a private commercial contract. His comments follow reports that Musk ordered restrictions affecting Ukrainian military drones. Kyiv says the limits have weakened its defenses, while conflicting accounts persist over the White House’s involvement and who controls the service.

The disruption has put thousands of jobs at risk and caused estimated monthly losses exceeding $2.2 billion.

Peskov also dismissed recent European peace proposals as unlikely to contribute constructively to a settlement.

European media call for protecting grain exports, warn of potential NATO security implications, and debate Russia’s possible involvement. However, the perpetrators remain unconfirmed, with investigations needed before accusations are made.

Air Raid Alerts Stall Ukraine-Poland Border Crossings — Air-raid alerts are repeatedly interrupting border clearance between Ukraine and Poland, with freight drivers facing estimated waits of up to 40 hours at Dorohusk. Customs authorities said repeated security-related stoppages were slowing cross-border traffic.

The Kremlin said Putin would review the proposals.

No Talks on Ukraine’s Future Without Kyiv at the Table – Zelensky on Possible Trump-Putin-Xi Meeting — President Volodymyr Zelensky insists Ukraine must be represented in any negotiations concerning its future, responding to discussions of a possible summit between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. Speaking in Oslo, he also reported positive signals from Washington on security guarantees, the restoration of missile early-warning intelligence and further military assistance.

Trump Says Ukraine ‘Has to Want to Make a Deal’ as Witkoff Heads to Russia — Speaking to reporters at the White House on Tuesday, Oct. 20, US President Donald Trump said Ukraine must want to make a deal and claimed that Washington received nothing in return for its aid, despite Kyiv repeatedly backing ceasefire proposals. US Restores Intelligence to Ukraine as Witkoff Carries Peace Proposals to Putin — US intelligence sharing with Ukraine has resumed after a week of missed allied ballistic missile warnings, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday, Oct. 20, following talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, Norway. Japan Lifts 5-Year Restrictions on Ukrainian Poultry, Egg Imports — Japan has resumed imports of Ukrainian poultry, eggs and egg products after five years of import restrictions, Ukraine’s ambassador to Japan Yurii Lutovinov said on Monday, Oct. 19. The decision was formally agreed upon on Oct. 16, and it opens a new market for Ukrainian producers, while adding to growing cooperation between Kyiv and Tokyo.

Russia Hits Kyiv Cardiology Institute’s Operating Room — Russian forces struck an operating room in Kyiv’s Strazhesko Institute of Cardiology on Tuesday, Oct. 20, injuring one patient, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said. The strike marks the second time Russia targeted the heart center that serves patients nationwide, after a September 2025 strike killed two people there.

Russian Drones Hit Kyiv Medical Facilities in Daytime Raid — Russian drones struck Kyiv Tuesday afternoon, damaging medical facilities and scattering debris across several districts. The city’s military administration reported five people injured by 5 p.m., with the attack still underway. The Kyiv City Council denied reports that the North Bridge itself had been hit, while warning of traffic disruption near the crossing.

North Korea Shares ‘Proof of Life’ Photos Over Death Rumors of Kim Jong Un — Social media rumors that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un had died after suffering a brain hemorrhage were picked up by the international press. In response, Pyongyang’s state media reported on a visit with his daughter to a clothing and footwear exhibition.

Kallas Says US Negotiators Tried to Push Ukraine Into Surrender for 1.5 Years — EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused US negotiators of trying to push Ukraine into surrendering to Russia for around 1.5 years. Romanian Parliament Approves Pro-EU Govt After Months of Deadlock — Romania’s parliament approved Luca Niculescu’s pro-European government with 280 votes, ending months of political deadlock. Russia Resumes Diesel Exports to Turkey, Brazil Despite Export Ban — Reuters said Russia has resumed diesel shipments to its major buyers following Trump’s diesel deal, with one tanker departing for Turkey on Oct. 14 and another for Brazil two days later, around the time Kyiv resumed its refinery attacks. Kyiv-Chelm Train – One Reporter’s Experience — On Oct 16-17, a Kyiv Post reporter rode a train from Kyiv’s main rail station to Chelm Poland, a popular destination for connection trains for people travelling from Ukraine to Warsaw and other cities in Poland. Lavrov Claims Peace Deal Would Mean End of Zelensky’s ‘Regime’ — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov accused Zelensky of repeatedly derailing peace negotiations, citing the Minsk process, Istanbul talks and trilateral meetings in Abu Dhabi. Zelensky Lands in Norway for Peace Talks With Trump’s Envoy — President Volodymyr Zelensky has arrived in Norway for talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb. Trump envoy Jared Kushner will participate remotely, while Zelensky will also meet Norway’s king and parliamentary leaders.

Slovenian Company Unveils Anti-Drone System Based on War-Proven Turret in Ukraine — The Slovenian remote-controlled weapon station (RCWS) specialist Valhalla Turrets has introduced the “Skythunder” counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS). France Flails — France’s escalating protests expose a deepening clash over welfare spending, public debt and generational priorities. US Intel Still Flows But Missile Warnings May Lag, Zelensky Advisor Says — Presidential adviser Beskrestnov says that US intelligence continues to reach Ukraine, but warnings of Russian missile attacks can arrive just a minute before impact. Trust in Zelensky Rises to 57% After US Pressure, Poll Finds — A new Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KIIS) poll found that 57% of respondents trusted President Volodymyr Zelensky in interviews conducted Oct. 10-16, up from 43% in a smaller group surveyed on Oct. 8-9. KIIS said the increase likely reflects a “rally-around-the-flag” effect after the US-Russia diesel deal and pressure on Ukraine. In the overall October survey, 54% said they trusted Zelensky and 41% did not.

EU Considers Restricted Schengen Visas for Russian Tourists — The EU is considering broader use of territorially restricted visas for Russian tourists amid security concerns. The plan has been under discussion since summer 2026, with France and Italy reportedly opposing a broader ban. In 2025, the total number of Schengen tourist visas issued reached a record 477,878.
CARTOON: The Ghost of True Republicanism Haunts Today’s Imposter — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.
